parameters.content:
## Instagram product posts
Turns your Shopify products into Instagram posts: the real product photo in your own frame, a caption written from the product data, a person approves it in Slack, and a paced queue posts it through the official Instagram API. No AI touches the image, and no price goes on it.

### How it works
1. **Setup** creates the `instagram_posts` and `instagram_token` tables. **Connect** is a form where you paste your Instagram access token once.
2. **Draft** (every morning, and after each Approve or Skip) keeps `max_waiting` drafts in Slack: one post per product, oldest first. A vision model checks the main photo, a chat model writes the words, and **Check the post** builds the caption and flags anything that breaks a rule.
3. **Frame** is the web page for the image. **Render** screenshots it with Firecrawl and keeps the JPEG in Shopify Files.
4. **Review** takes Slack's clicks: Approve, Edit, Skip, Cancel. **Book** gives an approved post the next slot in your pace.
5. **Publish** (every 15 minutes) posts whatever is due through the Instagram API.
6. **Token** (weekly) refreshes your token before its 60 days run out. **Report** (Mondays) says what posted and when the queue runs dry.

### Setup
Credentials: Shopify (client ID and secret, `read_products`, `read_files`, `write_files`), Slack bot token and signing secret, Ollama, Firecrawl. Run Setup, publish the workflow, open the **Save your Instagram token** form and paste a token from your Meta app (Instagram API with Instagram Login). Set your Slack app's Request URL to **Slack button click**'s production URL. Full steps in the README.

### Customisation
Products, pace and caption rules are in **Draft settings** and **Book settings**. The frame is plain HTML in **Build the page** (colours, fonts and logo in **Frame settings**). Turn `require_approval` off to book posts without a person, once you trust the checks.

## 1. Setup (run once)
Creates `instagram_posts` and `instagram_token`. Running it again keeps them.

## 2. Connect Instagram (form)
Paste a long-lived access token from your Meta app. It's checked against Instagram, then saved with your account id. Only signed-in n8n users can open the form.

## 3. Draft (every morning, and after each Approve or Skip)
Keeps up to `max_waiting` drafts in Slack. One post per product, ever, oldest first. Vision model for the photo, chat model for the words, then the checks and the frame.

## 4. Card
One renderer for every state of a post (draft, scheduled, publishing, posted, skipped, failed). Posts a new card or updates the existing one.

## 5. Frame (web page)
The 1080 x 1350 page for the image, drawn from the saved row only. Open `?id=<post id>` in a browser to design it.

## 6. Render
Firecrawl screenshots the frame page, wsrv.nl turns it into a JPEG, Shopify Files keeps it at a lasting public URL. Instagram fetches it from there when the post goes out.

## 7. Review (Slack's Request URL)
Checks Slack's signature first. Approve books a slot, Edit opens a modal (a new headline redraws the frame), Skip means this product never gets a post, Cancel takes a scheduled post back to a draft.

## 8. Book
One slot after the last scheduled or posted post: a week divided by `posts_per_week`, jittered, inside posting hours. Only a draft or failed post with an image can be booked.

## 9. Publish (every 15 minutes)
One due post a run: create the media container, wait until Instagram says FINISHED, publish, read the permalink. Errors leave the post failed with the reason on the card.

## 10. Token (weekly)
Instagram tokens last 60 days. This refreshes yours every week and warns the log channel if it fails or is close to running out.

## 11. Report (Mondays)
What posted last week, what's scheduled and when the queue runs out, and how long drafts have been waiting.

### Posts to Instagram
Creates a real, public post. Test with one product on an account you don't mind, or set `first_slot_after` ahead and Cancel.

### Writes to Shopify Files
Adds one image file per post, and deletes the old one when a frame is redrawn.

### Your token is stored in a table
Anyone who can open this n8n instance can read `instagram_token`. Keep the instance private.

nodes.name: Write the post

messageValues.message:
=You write Instagram posts for {{ $('Draft settings').first().json.store_name }}, {{ $('Draft settings').first().json.store_description }}. The voice is someone who knows the products: plain-spoken, friendly, keen on good gear. You get one product. Reply with these lines and nothing else:
Headline: ...
Product line: ...
Hook: ...
Body: ...
Fact: ...
Fact: ...
Fact: ...
Hashtags: ...

Headline: the words on the image. Two short beats, each ending with a full stop, 12 to 28 characters in total, about what the product does for the owner or its standout feature. Examples of the shape: "Solar powered. No wiring." "Sharp at night. One cable." Only claims the product data supports.
Product line: brand, model and a short product type, then one or two key specs, joined with " · ". 55 characters at most.
Hook: one sentence, 60 to 120 characters, opening with what the owner gets. Talk to "you".
Body: two sentences, 120 to 260 characters: what it is, and the places and people it suits.
Fact: three lines, each one short fact from the product data, 4 to 12 words, no full stop.
Hashtags: 3 to {{ $('Draft settings').first().json.max_hashtags }} lowercase hashtags separated by spaces, specific to the product type, power or use. The brand only if it is this product's brand.

Rules:
- Only facts in the product data. Never add a spec, a number or a feature, and never call it something it is not.
- Calm and upbeat. No fear and no hype.
- Write model numbers as given.
- No price, links, emojis or phone numbers. Never mention the image, photo or post itself.
- Use contractions (it's, you'll) like people talk.
- Vary the wording from product to product. Never write "great fit", "solid choice", "perfect for" or "look no further".
- Write in {{ $('Draft settings').first().json.language }}. {{ $('Draft settings').first().json.style_rules }}
- Never use the long dash character.

nodes.notes: One call per product: headline, product line, hook, body, three facts, hashtags.
